report:
### Evidence Overview

Clinical evidence supports the claim that targeted acupuncture can reduce depression symptoms during pregnancy, offering a viable non-pharmacological option for women seeking alternatives or adjuncts to antidepressant medications.

Key findings from research include:

* **Randomized Controlled Trials:** A landmark randomized controlled trial led by Stanford University researchers investigated pregnant women meeting diagnostic criteria for major depressive disorder. Women who received depression-targeted acupuncture demonstrated significantly greater symptom reduction and higher response rates than those in control groups receiving non-targeted acupuncture or control therapies (https://journals.lww.com/greenjournal/fulltext/2010/03000/acupuncture_for_depression_during_pregnancy__a.7.aspx, https://med.stanford.edu/news/all-news/2010/02/acupuncture-lessens-depression-symptoms-during-pregnancy-study-shows.html).
* **Safety and Systematic Evidence:** Medical literature and systematic reviews on complementary therapies during pregnancy indicate that acupuncture is a promising, safe treatment for antenatal depression with minimal side effects when delivered by a licensed practitioner experienced in prenatal care (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3689180/, https://womensmentalhealth.org/posts/acupuncture-for-depression-during-pregnancy/).

### Conclusion

The evidence supports the claim. Depression-targeted acupuncture significantly reduces depressive symptoms during pregnancy compared to control interventions. While larger multi-center trials are recommended to further standardize protocols, current clinical data supports acupuncture as an effective, safe option for treating antenatal depression.

* https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3689180/
